trigger: On a federated DataNode, an admin hot-adds a data volume with reconfig dfs.datanode.data.dir. While FsDatasetImpl.addVolume loads the block pools on the new disk (a slow du, simulated by a latch in a GetSpaceUsed plugged in through fs.getspaceused.classname), the admin also runs refreshNamenodes with one nameservice removed, which shuts that block pool down.
reason: DataNode.refreshVolumes takes an nsInfos snapshot outside any lock (datanode/DataNode.java:1284-1289). FsDatasetImpl.addVolume calls prepareVolume, which registers per-pool storage, and later builder.build() (fsdataset/impl/FsDatasetImpl.java:515-561). Nothing serialises this with DataNode.shutdownBlockPool -> DataStorage.removeBlockPoolStorage (DataNode.java:2151-2170, DataStorage.java:1421). So build() looks up a block pool that is no longer in bpStorageMap and hits 'assert bpStorage != null' (DataStorage.java:259). With assertions off, the next line bpStorage.addStorageDir throws a NullPointerException. That unchecked error escapes addVolume's IOException cleanup: sd.unlock() is never called, the volume reference and lazy-persist thread are leaked, and the volume is never registered. refreshVolumes reports 'FAILED to ADD' (DataNode.java:1343-1347). A retry of the hot-add then finds the storage directory still locked by this JVM: Storage.tryLock catches OverlappingFileLockException and returns null, which leads to 'already locked' (common/Storage.java:950-956). The disk cannot be added until the DataNode restarts. Both admin operations are valid, and the latch only widens a window that real disk I/O can produce.
summary: A volume hot-add that races with block-pool removal (refreshNamenodes) fails with AssertionError/NPE in VolumeBuilder.build and leaves the new volume's storage directory locked, so the disk cannot be added until the DataNode restarts.
